course: 1C:Enterprise 8 Programming — from foundations to professional development
title: Retries and idempotency
goal: Handle redelivery and same-requestIDpayload conflicts without duplicate documents.

prerequisites.text: onec.p10; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.

sections.title: Delivery can repeat
paragraphs: A sender may miss the reply to an accepted request. Redelivery with the samerequestIDshould return the agreed result without another document. This differs from deduplicating similar names. Define the key’s sender/operation scope and retention policy.

Create an own operation with a fresh UUID key and 30 minutes. Store the key in the existing Comment field of a new synthetic request; it is not an account ID or an instruction to clear data. Repeats compare minutes/customer/service, not only key labels.

sections.title: Bind key to content
paragraphs: Store requestID, canonical payload semantics or hash, state and result reference. The sameIDwith different amounts is a conflict, not permission to overwrite the first request. Different JSON key order can have identical semantics; define hashing rules explicitly.

First reception creates a record, an equal repeat returns the same reference and a 31-minute conflict rolls back. An independent key query must find exactly one 30-minute effect. A transaction alone does not prove uniqueness for two concurrent first requests.

sections.title: Acceptance and result are atomic
paragraphs: Processing registry and created document need transactional consistency. MarkingDonebefore a failed write makes retries return a nonexistent result. Writing without registeringIDduplicates on retry. Concurrent repeats need key protection; external effects need a separate protocol.

Run the complete source in a separate own copy through the server module. Print ПовторТотЖе,КонфликтОтклонен,ОдинЭффект and retain the actual key/reference. Two preparation documents form a different set; three documents overall do not mean three operation effects.

sections.title: A case that distinguishes the wrong solution
paragraphs: This is a real sequential BSL experiment, not a production receiver. Concurrent receivers need a unique-key register/correct locking, atomic outcome storage and crash recovery. Diagram a lost response: unknown outcome requires state lookup or the same key, not a fresh UUID. These additional guarantees remain unproved.

code.source: After a lost response propose using a fresh UUID.
code.output: Reject: a new key can create a second effect; reconcile the earlier outcome.

paragraphs: Success is inferred from an unavailable environment. Separate actual observations from a planned advanced scenario and name edition limits.

practice.title: Retries and idempotency
practice.task: Investigate the separate adverse case without claiming an unavailable environment was tested. After a lost response propose using a fresh UUID.
practice.environment: Separate own synthetic infobase; retain the prior module and its backup. Studio and Sandbox optional.

steps.title: Preserve the starting state
steps.action: Close Enterprise. Export a DT backup from Administration → Dump infobase; restore it into a new empty directory and verify the actual path. Preserve earlier functions/fields.
steps.expected: Separate copy opens with the earlier records.
steps.troubleshooting: A new list name alone does not create another database directory.
steps.before: Own path, prior sources and a restorable backup identified.

steps.title: Add the complete server source
steps.action: Create a server/server-call module without Global or Privileged. Paste the complete source below outside other procedures; retain a single shared preparation function if already present.
steps.why: Database access has an explicit server boundary.
steps.expected: Definitions are module-level; no duplicate helper.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not paste definitions inside startup or into an arbitrary Studio file.
steps.before: Separate copy opens with the earlier records.

steps.title: Prepare and call the experiment
steps.why: Print every named result instead of accepting compilation alone.
steps.expected: Only the stated caller is inside the existing startup handler.
steps.troubleshooting: Keep one startup handler; ensure the common module is server-call enabled.
steps.before: Definitions are module-level; no duplicate helper.

steps.title: Save, update and run once
steps.action: Run once and compare the fields with the worked trace. K/31; Rejected;one 30 effect.
steps.why: Observe actual 1C data, not the browser diagram.
steps.troubleshooting: Record the first failed assertion and module/line. Do not change the expectation merely to get True.
steps.before: Only the stated caller is inside the existing startup handler.

steps.title: Retain both results
steps.action: Remove only the startup call. Use another copy for the adverse case and keep both protocols.
steps.why: Preserve provenance and avoid repeating data creation at every startup.
steps.expected: Original retained, negative experiment isolated, automatic caller removed.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not clear registers or delete old documents to make a total agree.
